title: ArcCivs .25 routed work vs .26 direct-to-work routing
assumptions: This is a source comparison: .25 physical work is reported active on Spawn; .26 source is not claimed built, delivered or activated.

Scenarios retain the prior .25 physical-work assessment: 1/10/16 participating cities, each modeled as a level 1/2/3 site with 1/2/3 assigned workers. Farm harvest, farm bread, forestry and quarry are alternatives, not a combined city forecast. Activity counts are explicit assumptions, not telemetry.

The .25 physical-work cycle started at TO_STORAGE and made a full storage/workplace round trip for each action. In .26, a non-null worldWork plan starts directly at the workplace and completes there. FARM action portions remain 3 seconds, mine cells 4 seconds, and tree felling max(6 seconds, 1 second per log). No route-time or world-clock measurements are available.

The matched comparison fixes completed work at 1/4/9 mature crop harvests or bread recipes, 1/2/3 tree cuts of assumed 4/12/128 logs, and 5/10/15 changed mine cells per participating city-day. Per-action item quantities and inputs are unchanged; exact native crop/ore drops remain world- and tool-dependent.

Farm harvest is limited to fully mature native crops. Tree stock and mine deposits are finite; the 128-log high tree is a maximum-size finite-world stress assumption, not a sustainable daily rate. Nominal sapling input assumes an ordinary one-root species at 1/2/3 saplings; DARK_OAK is a mutually exclusive alternative requiring 4/8/12 paid saplings for the same tree-cut counts. No native material or mature tree is minted.

Per-action paid inputs and native durability behavior are unchanged. More completed actions could increase daily inputs and tool wear, but no such realized increase is measured. Each qualifying committed NPC work action still adds one internal profession point with a separate 40-point worker-profession cap; internal points are not player XP and do not alter Vault or tokens.

Requested-tool sensitivity assumes one missing matching native tool is transferred per assigned worker per city-day (1/2/3). Before, this uses manual resident inventory transfer; after, the button performs the same one-item transfer. The selected tool is existing player inventory, metadata is preserved, and an existing resident main-hand tool moves into its bag. This is conserved item transfer, not an issuance or reward.

A route-share sensitivity assumes 10/30/60 percent of the old cycle wall time was storage travel. Removing that assumed share yields only a work-bound theoretical action-rate multiplier of 1.11x/1.43x/2.50x. Natural growth, finite resources, viewers, stock, storage, pathing and schedules can prevent the increase; these multipliers are not observed throughput.
Idle wandering uses a slower 0.55 speed modifier and resets footstep tracking, so idle wandering accrues no Trails wear. Decorative changes are cosmetic and create no item flow.

Direct Vault, premium-token and player-XP deltas are each zero before and after. No item-to-currency exchange or new price is assumed. EconomyShopGUI SELL remains current and the planned SELL-to-contract transition remains future; any changed indirect sale exposure from extra work is unmeasured.
